title: Member Specimen Kits at Household Draws — Mobile In-Home Collection Visit
content:
Specimen logistics Q&A, **Specimen Collection Appointments**.

**Why does a household member's rate carry a kit amount?** Each member's draw is packed in the same kit as the patient's specimen, so the member's rate carries a kit amount set by the service class of the patient's order, as the order's record in Laboratory Test Orders shows that class.

**What are the amounts?**

| Service class of the patient's order | Added to each member's rate (USD) |
|---|---|
| Esoteric Reference Testing | 4.00 |
| Hereditary & Reproductive Genetic Testing | 4.00 |
| Specialty Clinical Testing | 2.00 |
| Molecular Infectious Disease Testing | 2.00 |
| Clinical Toxicology Testing | 2.00 |
| Any other class (Routine Clinical Testing; Anatomic Pathology & Cytology) | Nothing |

**The clause in full.** When the patient's order is of the Esoteric Reference Testing or Hereditary & Reproductive Genetic Testing class each member's rate carries 4.00 more, when it is of the Specialty Clinical Testing, Molecular Infectious Disease Testing or Clinical Toxicology Testing class each member's rate carries 2.00 more, and for any other class nothing is added.

**Whose order sets the class?** The patient's order — the order the home visit collects — not any order of the household member.

**Example (hypothetical).** A Mobile In-Home Collection Visit collecting a Molecular Infectious Disease Testing order with two household members drawn: each member's rate carries 2.00 more.
